newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money unchanged at 3.05/07 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money unchanged at 3.05/07 pct.

text.p: German call money traded virtually unchanged on Friday as liquidity conditions remained in equilibrium after the Bundesbank's unexpectedly large injection of funds on Wednesday.
Rates traded between 3.05/07 percent at the end of the week, unchanged from Wednesday's levels. Markets were closed on Thursday for the Ascension holiday.
"Trading is dull and quiet," said one trader and another added, "it is a bridge day as many people used the Friday as an extra holiday."
On Wednesday the Bundesbank injected a net 3.5 billion marks into the system, exceeding market expectations.
But dealers were quick to add that the extra funds should not be interpreted to mean the Bundesbank might be considering nudging the money market rate, currently set at three percent, lower again.
While rates began the session around 3.07 percent, dealers said more and more bank were willing to unload funds toward the end of the morning, helping push rates slightly lower.
Few expected any sort of move higher this afternoon, especially as banks' reserve holdings were said to be ample.

On Wednesday banks held 41.4 billion marks after holding 38.7 billion marks on Tuesday. This helped raise the month's average holdings to 40.3 billion marks on Thursday after 39.9 billion marks on Wednesday.
Borrowings at the 4.50 percent emergency Lombard borrowing facility were neglible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.09100 percent on Friday after 3.09300 percent on Wednesday. There was no fixing on Thursday due to the holiday.
